title: The global principle of word forms
summary: Only verbs, adjectives and the copula change, they change only their last kana, and they always do it by the same stem-and-helper system.

blocks.text: Until now you met the stem system one piece at a time. This lesson puts the whole picture in one place. Japanese has two kinds of words: **static words**, which never change (nearly all nouns), and **active words**, which can be an engine: verbs, adjectives and the **copula**. Every active word follows the same two rules.

items: **Only the last kana changes.** Everything before it is as fixed as a noun: the う-row kana of a verb, the い of an adjective, the だ of the copula.
**Every change is a stem with a helper.** The て-form and the past are not magic conjugations: a stem is made, then a helper (-て, -た, -ない, -ば, -そう ...) is attached.

blocks.text: You already know the first one (あ, い, う, え, お stems). The second is the **て-stem**, which is used for -て, -た and also -たら and -たり. The last kana decides the stem:
An adjective drops its い or turns it into か, け or く. Each stem takes its own helpers.

rows: ない, て, and alone as an adverb
高く, 高くない, 高くて

blocks.en: (I) run fast. (the く-stem as an adverb)

blocks.jp: 昨日の映画は面白かった。

blocks.en: If it is cheap, (I) will buy it.

blocks.jp: 弟はおもちゃを欲しがる。
blocks.en: My little brother shows signs of wanting a toy.

blocks.text: The copula だ is one kana, so it borrows a rider: だっ + た = だった, だろ + う = だろう, and its て-form is で. It is less regular because it has no relatives to be regular with.
今日は休みだった。 Today was a day off.

items: Nouns never change; they only take particles.
Verbs, adjectives and the copula change only their last kana, always by stem plus helper.

questions.note: Those three are the engines; nouns are static.

questions.instruction: Which part of a verb can change?
questions.note: Everything before the last kana is fixed.

questions.prompt: 昨日のカレーは＿＿。 (The curry yesterday was delicious.)

questions.note: く becomes い in the て-stem.
ぬ, ぶ, む become ん, and て softens to で.

questions.prompt: この犬は＿＿走る。 (This dog runs fast.)
questions.note: The く-stem on its own makes an adverb.
The け stem takes the rider れ before ば.
安く is the く-stem of 安い, working as an adverb.

questions.prompt: If it is expensive, I will not buy it.
questions.note: 高い → 高けれ + ば.

questions.prompt: A noun can change its ending the way a verb does.
questions.note: Nouns are static: they only take particles.

questions.instruction: What does 欲しがる describe?
questions.note: The zero stem of 欲しい + がる.

questions.instruction: Which is the て-form of the copula?
questions.note: だ → で; だっ and だろ are stems for -た and -う.
